ui.title: Drive diagnostics
ui.selfWarning: Self-tests may worsen recovery chances on failing drives.

report.title: Drive diagnostics
report.warning: For failing drives, prioritize backup or gentle data recovery before additional stress tests.
report.notice: SMART snapshot, not a full surface test. A passing SMART status does not guarantee working hardware.
report.textSelectedDiagnosticValuesRawValuesMay: Selected diagnostic values. Raw values may use vendor-specific encodings.
report.textExtractOfAvailableEntriesNotThe: Extract of available entries, not the complete error history.
report.textReportBasedOnSmartAndOperating: Report based on SMART and operating-system information available at the time of capture.

findings.testsHistorical: {count} earlier self-test failure(s), superseded by a successful extended test.
findings.testsInterrupted: {count} self-test(s) aborted or interrupted; no proven media error.
findings.packedUnclear: Attribute {id}: raw value cannot be reliably decoded.
findings.vendorRaw: SMART {id} ({name}): vendor-specific packed raw value; no reliable error count can be derived.
findings.thresholdPast: SMART attribute {id} crossed its threshold in the past.
findings.nvmeCommandErrors: {count} recently read NVMe entries involve invalid or unsupported commands.
findings.nvmeOtherErrors: {count} NVMe error entries need further examination.
findings.nvmeLogMedia: {count} NVMe error entries indicate media or data integrity failures.
findings.nvmeLogPartial: Only {count} entries examined out of {total} cumulative NVMe error events.
findings.reallocationEvents: SMART 196 – reallocation events: {count} reported by the drive. This is not necessarily the number of defective sectors.
findings.ataCrcHistory: SMART 199: {count} historical CRC interface errors. This counter alone does not indicate a current media defect.
findings.ssdProgramFailures: SMART {id}: {count} program failures reported by the SSD controller. Units are vendor-specific.
findings.ssdEraseFailures: SMART {id}: {count} erase failures reported by the SSD controller. Units are vendor-specific.
findings.ssdReservedBlocksUsed: SMART {id}: {count} reserved blocks reported as used. Not a direct count of defective user-data sectors.
findings.ssdRuntimeBadBlocks: SMART {id}: {count} runtime bad blocks reported by the SSD controller.
findings.ssdPackedErrorCounter: SMART {id}: vendor-encoded SSD error counter. An exact count cannot be determined reliably.
findings.ssdFlashBlockHistory: SMART {id}: {count} blocks reported as “Added Bad Flash Blocks”. Vendor history alone does not prove a current user-data error.
findings.ssdPackedFlashBlocks: SMART {id}: packed vendor-specific flash-block value. Count and meaning are ambiguous.
findings.ssdReserveLow: SSD reports {spare}% available spare against a device threshold of {threshold}%.
findings.ssdEnduranceUsed: SSD reports {used}% endurance consumed. This is a device estimate, not a calculated remaining lifetime.
findings.ata_crc_history: Historical interface CRC errors: {count}. Check cable/USB bridge and trends.
findings.nvme_spare_low: NVMe reports a spare-capacity warning (Critical Warning).
findings.nvme_temperature_warning: NVMe reports a critical temperature warning.
findings.nvme_read_only: NVMe switched to read-only mode; regular operation is no longer reliable.
findings.nvme_unknown_warning_bits: NVMe warning bits {count} are not understood; verify manufacturer information.
findings.nvme_invalid_warning_mask: Invalid NVMe critical-warning field ({count}); cannot reliably interpret it.
findings.nvme_spare_threshold: NVMe available spare is at or below the manufacturer threshold ({count}%).
findings.nvme_endurance_used: NVMe reports {count}% of estimated endurance used; this does not predict failure.
findings.temperature_critical_limit: Current temperature ({count}°C) reaches the device-reported critical limit.
findings.temperature_operating_limit: Current temperature ({count}°C) reaches the reported operating limit.
findings.temperature_near_operating_limit: Current temperature ({count}°C) approaches the reported operating limit.
findings.ata_unc_history: ATA error log contains {count} UNC entries (historical uncorrectable read failures; recency unverified).

recommendations.noData: Check SMART access and device connection. The available data is insufficient for a reliable assessment.
recommendations.critical: Back up important data immediately. If read errors are present, avoid stress tests before backup or appropriate recovery.
recommendations.warning: Verify current backups, investigate warnings and compare results in a follow-up check.
recommendations.ok: No abnormalities in evaluated indicators. Continue regular backups.
recommendations.nvme: NVMe logs contain command errors or only partially retrieved history. Do not interpret them as media failures without additional evidence.
recommendations.limited: SMART data retrieval was limited. The assessment is based only on available information.
recommendations.ataCrcHistory: Compare the CRC counter at the next reading. If it rises, check the data cable, connections and any USB adapter.
recommendations.selfTestInterrupted: An aborted or interrupted self-test does not prove media damage. If necessary, repeat an appropriate test after ensuring a backup.
recommendations.uiPermissionDenied: The operating system denied access to this drive. On Windows, restart DriveNX with administrator privileges. If the error persists, check device permissions and security software.
recommendations.uiNoData: No reliable SMART assessment available. Check device access and the USB adapter; try another connection if necessary.
recommendations.uiUrgent: Back up data promptly, avoid unnecessary drive activity and investigate the SMART finding. Plan a replacement if media errors are confirmed.
recommendations.uiCritical: Back up data and investigate the critical SMART findings. Distinguish historical errors from current values; plan replacement if appropriate.
recommendations.uiWarning: Verify backups, document the SMART findings and compare them with a later reading.
recommendations.uiCrc: Historical CRC interface errors do not prove a current media defect. Compare the counter at the next reading and check connections, cables and any USB adapter if it increases.
recommendations.uiInterrupted: Aborted or interrupted self-tests do not establish a media defect. Repeat a supported test if appropriate, after ensuring data is backed up.
recommendations.uiNvme: Review the NVMe error log. Invalid commands alone do not prove media failure; only part of the historical log may be available.
recommendations.uiLimited: Available SMART indicators are unremarkable. Some supplementary logs were unavailable; this alone does not indicate a drive failure.
recommendations.uiOk: No specific action is required based on the available SMART indicators. Maintain regular backups and compare trends at a later check.
recommendations.uiObserve: Compare readings at the next check and watch for changes. Verify existing backups.
recommendations.observe: Monitor historical or minor findings and document any changes.

preferences.title: Preferences
preferences.autoReadNotice: Off by default: avoids unnecessary access and waking other drives. The selected drive is still read.
preferences.smartToolNotice: DriveNX uses a fixed smartctl binary.
preferences.autoHistoryNotice: Stores completed SMART reads locally, including other-drive background reads if enabled. No continuous monitoring.
preferences.autoBackupHistoryNotice: Optional: create a separate local copy per drive after saving. Data stays on this computer.

smartView.scsiCounterExplanation: These are cumulative uncorrected read, write and verify errors, not individual error-log events. Unavailable counters are shown as unknown.
smartView.unknownRaw: Vendor-specific raw value; no reliable error count can be inferred.
smartView.headerCurrent: Current: normalized present SMART value. Higher values are usually better, but the scale is vendor-specific.
smartView.headerWorst: Worst: lowest historical normalized value reported for this attribute.
smartView.headerThreshold: Threshold: vendor-defined limit. Crossing it marks the attribute as critical.
smartView.headerRaw: Raw: original counter or vendor value. The encoding can vary by manufacturer and model.
smartView.historyDescription: Up to 100 measurements per verified drive. With automatic history enabled, background reads are saved as well. Import/export is for backup, not proof of authenticity.
smartView.historyIdentityMissing: No stable device identity: model or serial number missing.
smartView.historyNote: Changes are not automatic fault assessments. Falling cumulative counters may indicate a reset or a replacement.
smartView.historyRawNote: Compare raw data as well: counters may reset, and vendor-specific multi-field raw values are intentionally omitted.
smartView.attributeInterpretationNote: Device value reported by smartctl; interpretation and units may depend on the manufacturer.
smartView.noSelfTestsSupported: This drive does not support SMART self-tests.
smartView.nvmeErrorDetails: NVMe error counter and available log entries; stored detail rows may be fewer than the total count.
smartView.overviewControllerLimit: Controller-defined temperature limits; see SMART assessment separately.
smartView.overviewTemperatureHint: Indicative temperature range, not a manufacturer-specific limit.
smartView.overviewNvmeDataHint: NVMe data units (1 unit = 512,000 bytes); lifetime total.
smartView.overviewWearHint: Reported estimated endurance consumption, if reliable. Not a probability of failure.
smartView.overviewNoUniversalWrites: Transfer volumes cannot be derived reliably from the available SMART values for this device without vendor-specific rules.
smartView.overviewHistoricalCounter: Lifetime counter; not evidence of a fault by itself.
smartView.overviewNoFindings: No critical SMART findings in the current assessment.
smartView.overviewNoReliableAssessment: A complete health assessment is not available.
smartView.overviewMoreFindings: Additional findings: {count}. See Overview for details.
smartView.overviewReadoutPartial: SMART data could not be read completely.
smartView.plausibilityNote: Potentially inconsistent measurements. Not proof of tampering or drive failure.
smartView.plausibility_zeroHoursWithIo: Zero power-on hours despite significant NVMe read/write counters
smartView.plausibility_counterDecreased: A normally cumulative counter decreased (reset, replacement or read error possible)
smartView.trimOsNotice: Global Windows file-system configuration. This does not prove TRIM passes through a USB adapter.
smartView.macIoNotice: Cumulative macOS host I/O counters (e.g., since device initialization). Shown only with a unique device match; not a drive speed measurement.
smartView.macIoUnknown: No host I/O counters uniquely attributable to this drive.
smartView.autoHistoricTransportEventsIsolatedReset: Historic transport events; isolated resets do not prove a current defect. Overflowed counters are not valid lifetime totals.
smartView.autoAllReadOutSATAPHYCounters: All read-out SATA PHY counters are zero or unavailable.
smartView.autoAllSATAPHYCountersIncludingZero: All SATA PHY counters including zero values
smartView.autoAvailableLogAreasPresenceOfA: Available log areas; presence of a log does not indicate an error. Vendor-specific entries are grouped separately.
smartView.autoEnduranceUsedInCurrentSmartctlReadou: Endurance used in current smartctl readout
smartView.autoDeviceReportedValuesNotACalculated: Device-reported values, not a calculated remaining lifetime. Separate reads may disagree.
smartView.autoIndependentDeviceStatisticsHistorica: Independent device statistics. Historical counters are not additional SMART attributes. Invalid values are never interpreted as zero.
smartView.autoTheDetailedErrorLogCouldNot: The detailed error log could not be read. A zero lifetime counter does not mean the log page was successfully read.
smartView.autoNotEveryHistoricalErrorStillHas: Not every historical error still has a readable detail record.
smartView.autoTechnicalDetailsAndPreviousATAComman: Technical details and previous ATA commands
smartView.autoNVMeErrorLogUnavailableSMARTHealth: NVMe error log unavailable (SMART health data may still be available).
smartView.ataMetricResetsBetweenCmdAcceptanceAndCo: Resets Between Cmd Acceptance and Completion
smartView.ataPhyCommandFailedDueToIcrcError: Command failed due to ICRC error
smartView.ataPhyRErrResponseForDeviceToHostDataFis: R_ERR response for device-to-host data FIS
smartView.ataPhyRErrResponseForHostToDeviceDataFis: R_ERR response for host-to-device data FIS
smartView.ataPhyRErrResponseForDeviceToHostNonData: R_ERR response for device-to-host non-data FIS
smartView.ataPhyRErrResponseForHostToDeviceNonData: R_ERR response for host-to-device non-data FIS
smartView.ataPhyTransitionFromDrivePhyrdyToDrivePh: Transition from drive PhyRdy to drive PhyNRdy
smartView.ataPhyDeviceToHostRegisterFisesSentDueTo: Device-to-host register FISes sent due to a COMRESET
smartView.ataPhyRErrResponseForHostToDeviceDataFis: R_ERR response for host-to-device data FIS, CRC
R_ERR response for host-to-device data FIS, non-CRC
smartView.ataPhyRErrResponseForHostToDeviceNonData: R_ERR response for host-to-device non-data FIS, CRC
R_ERR response for host-to-device non-data FIS, non-CRC
smartView.ataTemperatureAboveLimit: The stored lifetime maximum ({maximum} °C) exceeds the reported operating limit ({limit} °C). Timing and current cause are unknown.
smartView.ataTemperatureSamplesSummary: {valid} valid samples, {missing} missing. This is a distribution, not a time series.
smartView.ataTemperatureRingBuffer: Original SCT circular-buffer slot order; no reconstructed wall-clock timestamps. Sampling: {sampling} min, logging: {logging} min, missing: {missing}, buffer index: {index}, declared slots: {slots}.
smartView.selfTestSupportUnknown: SMART self-test support could not be confirmed. Starting a test is disabled.
smartView.macUsbScsiReadUnavailable: SMART data could not be read through the USB/SCSI (UASP) connection on macOS. The adapter may not pass through the required SMART commands. Device information is still supplied by macOS; this alone does not indicate a drive failure.
smartView.selfTestStarted: SMART self-test started. Check its status under Self-tests (refresh to read again).
smartView.historyChartSamplingNote: Points represent saved measurements; no continuous monitoring takes place between them.
smartView.startupErrorInstructions: Please provide the error details and startup.log for troubleshooting.
smartView.errorLbaOutsideCapacity: The logged LBA {lba} exceeds the reported device address range (valid LBA 0–{maximum}). This access alone does not prove media damage.
smartView.accessModeNote: For this discovered drive only. An incompatible mode can lead to long waits or failed reads.
smartView.accessModeReset: A new scan uses automatic detection or the previously selected USB profile again.
smartView.accessModeHybridNotice: Hybrid mode: smartctl first attempts NVMe Identify, then falls back to SAT if that fails. This can take considerably longer for SATA. When SATA is already identified, select “sat” directly.
smartView.scanModeSubtitle: For checking several SATA or NVMe SSDs through the same adapter.
smartView.scanModeNote: Automatic detection lists devices with --scan first. Ambiguous JMicron/Realtek USB bridges require choosing SATA/NVMe before a hardware access; other devices are also checked with --scan-open. A fixed USB profile applies to the current scan.
smartView.deviceAccessSubtitle: Automatic discovery and targeted smartctl access types in one place.
smartView.deviceAccessNoSelection: After discovery, you can choose a different smartctl driver for the selected drive here.
smartView.attributeStatusExplanation: Only findings supported by the diagnostic algorithm are highlighted. No individual finding does not mean the drive is healthy.
smartView.attributeLimitedReadout: SMART data is incomplete. Other problems cannot be ruled out.
smartView.attributeUnlinkedFindings: Other diagnosis findings involve self-tests, error logs or global values. See the overview for details.
smartView.attributeNoFindings: No individually linked findings in this table.
smartView.attributeDiagnosisReasonUnknown: Finding reported by the diagnostic algorithm; see the overview for details.
smartView.attributeNoEvidence: There is no individual diagnostic finding for this metric. This does not imply the entire drive is healthy.
smartView.attributeRawHelp: Vendor values are not a universal percentage. Normalized values are compared to the vendor threshold; raw data can be a counter or proprietary encoding.
smartView.coverageCompleteHelp: Core SMART indicators needed for assessment are available.
smartView.coverageOptionalHelp: Core health indicators could be assessed. An optional SMART command or log was unavailable. This alone is not a drive failure.
smartView.coverageIncompleteHelp: Important health indicators are missing. The diagnosis is based only on available evidence.
smartView.overviewWearContext: Estimated endurance consumed, not failure probability
smartView.selfTestEmptyUnsupported: This drive does not expose startable SMART self-tests through smartctl. This is a capability limitation, not proof of a defect. Use manufacturer diagnostics if needed.
smartView.selfTestEmptyUnknown: Self-test support cannot be reliably determined for this drive.
smartView.errorLogUnavailable: The detailed error log could not be read. A historical error counter does not replace log records.
smartView.errorLogNoRecords: No readable individual events in the available log.
smartView.usbChoiceText: Discovery suggests a USB-to-NVMe driver but does not confirm the installed drive type. Select the drive type. Unsupported access modes are not offered.
smartView.usbChoiceRisk: With smartctl 7.5 the combined mode tries NVMe first. Some bridges may hang or reset. Use only if the drive type is unknown.
smartView.usbChoiceApply: Apply drive type and read SMART
smartView.historyInsightNote: Only comparable saved readings. Not additional proof of failure or a prediction.
smartView.historyTrend_previousIncrease: Increased earlier, unchanged in the last reading
smartView.historyTrend_reset: Counter reset; series no longer comparable
smartView.historyTrend_insufficient: Not enough readings after counter reset
smartView.historyStableDays: No further increase for {days} days in the observed period
smartView.historyAction_inspectConnection: Check cable, adapter and connection; rescan for new errors.
smartView.historyAction_secureDataAndVerify: Secure data and verify media; avoid unnecessary write tests.
smartView.historyAction_verifyMedia: A decrease does not establish repair. Continue investigating.
smartView.autoBackupHistoryNotice: Optional: create a separate local copy per drive after saving. Data stays on this computer.
smartView.historyBackupAvailable: A separate local backup of the history is available.
smartView.plausibility_wearDecreased: Reported consumed endurance decreased; check model and firmware interpretation
smartView.plausibility_spareIncreased: Reported available spare increased; check vendor-specific meaning
smartView.historyBackupDamaged: The local history backup is damaged or unreadable. The regular measurement history is still available.
smartView.overviewWearConflict: Conflicting endurance data: SMART reports {reported} %, vendor-derived {inferred} %. No single reliable value can be established.
smartView.historyRestoreConfirmNote: The backup will be merged into the current history only after confirmation.
smartView.usbChoiceBridgeHint: USB bridge (SMART access type not yet confirmed)
smartView.usbChoiceDriverUnavailable: No supported NVMe access mode is available for this USB NVMe driver. Choose later and inspect advanced SMART access modes. Do not choose SATA if the installed drive is NVMe.
smartView.scsiLifetimeErrors: Uncorrected errors recorded over the device lifetime.

ata.1.label: Read error rate
ata.1.interpretation: Raw encoding is vendor-specific; do not treat as a count without model-specific rules.

ata.3.label: Spin-up time
ata.3.description: Time or vendor-specific indicator for HDD spin-up.
ata.3.interpretation: Raw units depend on the model.

ata.4.label: Start/stop count
ata.4.interpretation: Usage context, not a stand-alone fault indicator.

ata.5.label: Reallocated sectors
ata.5.description: Problematic storage areas remapped by the drive.
ata.5.interpretation: An increase can signal media problems. Packed raw data is not a direct count.

ata.7.label: Seek error rate
ata.7.description: Vendor-specific indicator of HDD seek errors.
ata.7.interpretation: Do not compare raw values without vendor definitions.

ata.10.label: Spin retry count
ata.10.interpretation: Investigate mechanics and power if increases are confirmed.

ata.12.label: Power cycles
ata.12.interpretation: Usage metric, not a stand-alone health verdict.

ata.177.label: Wear leveling count
ata.177.interpretation: For Samsung this is model-dependent; 98 is not automatically 98% remaining life.

ata.179.label: Used reserved blocks
ata.179.description: SSD controller reserve blocks in use.
ata.179.interpretation: Use with known Samsung profile; not equivalent to NVMe spare percentage.

ata.182.label: Erase failures
ata.182.description: SSD flash erase operations reporting errors.

ata.187.label: Reported uncorrectable errors
ata.187.interpretation: Large or packed raw values must not be interpreted as direct counts.

ata.188.label: Command timeouts
ata.188.description: Commands that did not finish in time.
ata.188.interpretation: Can also relate to interface, cable or power; raw value is often packed.

ata.190.label: Airflow temperature
ata.190.interpretation: Raw value can contain min/max information.

ata.191.label: Shock events
ata.191.description: Events recorded by the shock sensor.

ata.192.label: Power-off retracts
ata.192.description: Head retracts on power loss or similar events.

ata.193.label: Load/unload cycles
ata.193.interpretation: High values relative to hours may matter, but no universal failure threshold.

ata.196.label: Reallocation events
ata.196.description: Events related to remapping storage areas.
ata.196.interpretation: On HDDs correlate with attribute 5 and error log.

ata.197.label: Pending sectors
ata.197.description: Sectors awaiting resolution after read problems.
ata.197.interpretation: Confirmed positive counts on HDDs are particularly relevant.

ata.198.label: Offline uncorrectable sectors
ata.198.description: Uncorrectable sectors found in offline tests.
ata.198.interpretation: On HDDs investigate and protect data before stress testing.

ata.199.label: Interface CRC errors
ata.199.description: Transmission errors between device and host.
ata.199.interpretation: Often cabling or connection; isolated historic counts do not prove media damage.

nvme.critical_warning.label: Critical warnings
nvme.critical_warning.description: NVMe bitfield for current critical conditions.

nvme.temperature.label: Temperature
nvme.temperature.interpretation: Compare with device-specific limits when available.

nvme.available_spare.label: Available spare
nvme.available_spare.interpretation: Critical below reported threshold; not comparable to ATA spare-block counts.

nvme.available_spare_threshold.label: Spare threshold
nvme.available_spare_threshold.interpretation: Compare the model-specific threshold directly to available spare. Apple may report 99%; do not substitute a universal 10% threshold.

nvme.percentage_used.label: Endurance used
nvme.percentage_used.interpretation: 100% is an endurance estimate, not an immediate failure; values can exceed 100%.

nvme.data_units_read.label: Data units read
nvme.data_units_read.description: NVMe data units, typically 512,000 bytes each.
nvme.data_units_read.interpretation: Read volume, not a fault metric.

nvme.data_units_written.label: Data units written
nvme.data_units_written.description: NVMe data units, typically 512,000 bytes each.
nvme.data_units_written.interpretation: Write volume; no universal remaining-life percent without TBW specification.

nvme.num_err_log_entries.label: Error log entries
nvme.num_err_log_entries.interpretation: Not every entry means media failure.

nvme.unsafe_shutdowns.label: Unsafe shutdowns
nvme.unsafe_shutdowns.description: Shutdowns without the expected shutdown notification.
nvme.unsafe_shutdowns.interpretation: Historic indicator, not automatically hardware damage.

usbConnection.nameFromTheDeviceIdentifier: Name from the device identifier; not verified as a specific controller model.
usbConnection.usbConnectionDetectedTheActual: USB connection detected. The actual device path could not be reliably identified.

usbConnection.availableUSBSpeedValuesAre: Available USB speed values are shown. Only the SATA maximum is known, not the current link speed. A bottleneck cannot be confirmed.
usbConnection.availableSpeedValuesAreShown: Available speed values are shown on the relevant connections. More link data is required to assess bottlenecks.
usbConnection.reportedMaximumNotNecessarilyThe: Reported maximum; not necessarily the current negotiated speed
usbConnection.osUsbSpeed: USB speed reported by the operating system
usbConnection.idAmbiguous: ID shared by multiple adapter variants
usbConnection.trimIsReportedByThe: TRIM is reported by the drive; USB adapter passthrough was not tested separately.
usbConnection.usbStorageDriver: USB mass-storage driver; UASP not confirmed
usbConnection.scsiInquiryBridgeName: SCSI device name (may identify the USB enclosure)
usbConnection.usbSpeedLimited: USB link speed could not be reliably determined. The SATA rate refers to the internal drive link, not USB throughput.

linuxDependencies.title: DriveNX – Linux requirements
linuxDependencies.bothMissing: smartctl and the pkexec authorization tool are missing.
linuxDependencies.smartctlMissing: smartctl is not installed or could not be found in a trusted system location.
linuxDependencies.pkexecMissing: The pkexec authorization tool is not available.
linuxDependencies.explanation: DriveNX requires smartmontools for drive diagnostics. On Linux, it uses pkexec (Polkit) for privileged hardware access when available. The application itself never runs as root.
linuxDependencies.installManual: Install smartmontools and, if needed, pkexec/Polkit through your Linux distribution’s package manager.
linuxDependencies.agentNote: Graphical authorization also requires an active Polkit authentication agent. Restart DriveNX after installation. No system packages are installed automatically.
